solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink I raise facing sun with period of time on the sidelines?

indicators.note: the period of time stands at the edges, either side of the other letters, as if watching from the sidelines

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
to sky a ball is to hit it high into the air, i.e. raise it

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a drink while sitting out in the sunshine, idly passing time away from the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the sidelines' sets the period of time at both edges of the rest. 'Raise' looks like lifting a glass, but it is the cricket sense of hitting a ball high in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail of spirit, lemon juice and sugar is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: Caribbean engineers make communication

parts.note: WI stands for the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers from the Caribbean set up a link so messages can be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is called this, so the word serves as a dated term for a message or communication.

clue.text: Spirited driver's first with a lot of speed turning up in this?

definitions.text: Spirited driver's first with a lot of speed turning up in this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: racy means lively or spirited

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word driver's is taken
most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly, to speed along

explanation.surface: A lively driver with plenty of speed comes into view: what is he racing in?
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last letter of NIP, leaving NI; RACY, D and NI are then reversed by 'turning up'. The whole clue also describes the answer: a spirited driver going fast is in one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an American single-seater racing car, the kind a fast, spirited driver competes in.

clue.text: Man getting food produced in upturn during years for noted race

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
tuck is British slang for food, especially snacks at school

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the two years, during them

parts.note: Y is an abbreviation for year, so two of them give years

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: bred means produced, as of animals

explanation.surface: A man finds food at an event in a year of revival, ahead of a famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In upturn' turns the word for produced upwards, giving DERB, and 'during' sets it between the two Ys. The food word is British schoolboy slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This horse race at Churchill Downs, Louisville, is the most famous event in American flat racing.

clue.text: Instant record showing game's exciting

parts.note: snap is a children's card game; with the 's it gives the letters plus S
hot can mean exciting or sensational

explanation.surface: A record set in a game has been broken, and the result is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph taken on the spur of the moment is an instant record of a scene.

clue.text: Complete mess Sri Lanka ignored

indicators.note: the letters for the country are left out of the word for mess

parts.note: clutter is an untidy mess
CL is the international vehicle registration code for Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: A total shambles in which Sri Lanka gets overlooked, perhaps by cricket selectors.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means total or absolute, as in a complete fool.

clue.text: Exchange in prisoners recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Prisoners are summoned back as part of a swap between two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of swap, meaning to trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Dispute produced by Republican in crafty exercise

indicators.note: the party letter goes inside the word for crafty exercise

parts.note: to wangle is to get something by crafty means, a crafty exercise

explanation.surface: A political row is started by a Republican in some cunning manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue noisily or at length is to dispute, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Chatter on the rise? It's not a ground or place for speaking among Americans

indicators.note: in a down clue the word rises, being read from bottom to top

parts.note: to yap is to chatter

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters are crushed and remade

explanation.surface: Chatter is going up: this is not a sports ground, nor a place to talk in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun (a sports ground) but is the anagram signal for IT'S NOT A, giving STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this term for a public telephone or call-box, a place for speaking on the phone.

clue.text: Bust indoors not extra large — by him?

definitions.text: Bust indoors not extra large — by him?

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letters for extra large are left out of the word indoors

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, extra large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A bust kept inside, not an outsize one: was it sculpted by him?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes O and S from INDOORS, and 'Bust' rearranges INDOR. Read whole, the clue points to the sculptor of busts.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor, made many busts, so a bust may well be by him.

clue.text: A set of old books I extract with no end of fervour?

definitions.text: A set of old books I extract with no end of fervour?

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of old books of the Bible

indicators.note: the chosen letter is dropped from the word for extract

parts.note: to quarry is to extract stone or information

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word fervour is meant

explanation.surface: A collector describes digging out a set of old books with endless enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no end of fervour' takes R, the last letter of fervour, out of QUARRY. Read whole, the clue pictures a collector of old things.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector or student of antiques and old books, who would eagerly hunt out an old set.

clue.text: What could be scribbled in a note's found among some papers — statistician's material?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the word for some papers

parts.note: a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

indicators.note: written hastily and messily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something written down hastily in a note is found in a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scribbled' jumbles IN A NOTE'S into ESTIONNA, and 'found among' sets that inside the paper measure of 24 or 25 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey form of set queries is the raw data source a statistician analyses.

clue.text: One seeking belt transformed rig with rescue

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oil rig is changed by the addition of rescue equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' suggests a seatbelt or a blow; here it is a boxing champion's belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in this weight class would fight to win a championship belt.

clue.text: Unconventional way to describe places near centre of old Berlin?

definitions.text: way to describe places near centre of old Berlin?
definitions.meaning: from 1961 to 1989 the Berlin Wall ran near the city centre, so nearby places were literally beside it

explanation.surface: An offbeat way of describing streets close to the middle of Cold War Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bizarre or eccentric; literally it can describe spots beside the old Berlin barrier.

clue.text: Secure establishment conflicted, we hear, with theologian

indicators.note: the word is as it sounds when spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: fought means took part in a conflict
John Knox was the Scottish Protestant reformer and theologian

explanation.surface: A secure institution was torn by conflict, apparently, in the presence of a theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match works in British speech, where the R in the first word is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Bullion Depository in Kentucky is a famously secure installation guarding gold reserves.

clue.text: A cricket match full of runs becoming leisurely

indicators.note: the abbreviation for runs goes inside the word for cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A high-scoring cricket match turns into a relaxed, unhurried affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a multi-day international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means relaxed and still, not busy, so it can describe someone taking things easy.

clue.text: What domestic minder may do with success protecting old customs?

indicators.note: the word for success wraps around the other letters, guarding them

parts.note: a hit is a success
uses are customs or habitual practices

explanation.surface: A home help succeeds while preserving long-established household traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking after a home while the owners are away stays there and guards it.

clue.text: On reflection, Miliband with skill restricts one making offensive speech

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Ed Miliband, Labour leader at the time

indicators.note: the word for skill holds the numeral within it

parts.note: art means skill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, Ed Miliband skilfully curbs someone giving an insulting speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns the whole string round, ARIT included. Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, angry, abusive speech is a harangue, an offensive outburst.

clue.text: Film, perhaps, much of dance around meadows

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the word for meadows
most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: A film, perhaps, features a long dance sequence circling through grassy fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A new film put out to cinemas is called this, so a film is an example; hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pass men with trouble in state

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Soldiers have difficulty getting through a mountain pass in some US state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty US states, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Part of clothing found in a jolly secret place

parts.note: jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
a hole can be a hidden spot or hideaway

explanation.surface: A piece of a garment is discovered tucked into a cheerful hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, cheerful, but is naval slang for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a garment through which the arm passes is a part of clothing.

clue.text: Motto that's blue in rumpus spread around university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for university
spread out and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slogan featuring the word blue causes an uproar that spreads across campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of BLUE IN RUMPUS are placed around U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase 'out of many, one' appears on the US Great Seal as its traditional motto.

clue.text: Indian food taken up among unfit labourers

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, in reverse
the letters sit inside the words unfit labourers

explanation.surface: A curry is carried upstairs to workers who are out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of curry cooked and served in a metal pan, popular in British Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Burden, we hear, is something attractive to soldiers?

indicators.note: the word for burden is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a yoke is a burden or oppressive load

explanation.surface: A burden, rumour has it, is something troops find appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The runny centre of a boiled egg is what toast strips are dipped into, hence drawn to them.

clue.text: A soft sheep going over plant

indicators.note: turned over, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: soft can mean foolish or silly
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A gentle sheep tumbles over a plant in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' turns the two words together into MARYLLIS; 'soft' here means foolish, not gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulbous flowering plant with large trumpet blooms, the belladonna lily.

clue.text: Club largely sealing approval for exotic tree

indicators.note: the trimmed word encloses the letters for approval, sealing them in
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A golf club mostly made of wood from a foreign tree gets the nod.
explanation.definitionFit: A large West African hardwood tree, sometimes called African teak, exotic to Britain.

clue.text: National symbol is close to bell with a frightening sound

indicators.note: the end of the word bell, its last letter

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: A national emblem rings out like a bell with a scary noise.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is the national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: At sea ketch hid half of tern and duck

indicators.note: all at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled
the first half of the word tern is used

explanation.surface: Out on the water, a sailing boat hid half a seabird and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a bird beside the tern, but it is the verb: to dodge by dropping down.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw oneself flat on the ground for cover is to duck, an idiomatic synonym.
